articles.title: How the Premier League transfer market has exploded
articles.summary: Has the football transfer market lost the plot? Sky Sports looks into why Premier League fees are soaring and if the trend is here to stay...
articles.body:
A trend started by Jack Grealish's £100m move from Aston Villa to Manchester City in 2021 has created a domino effect, establishing a new benchmark for elite Premier League talent that continues to send records tumbling.

Fees since have begun to accelerate far beyond general market inflation, with the average price for dipping into the premium player pool doubling over the past decade.

This clear acceleration has been particularly apparent over the past three years. Between 2016-2023, average top-end costs held relatively steady. They fluctuated to a degree but not with the disparity we see now.

Following on from Grealish, the idea of a £100m-plus investment became more normalised.

His sale, and to an extent that of Romelu Lukaku (£97.5m) around the same time, marked a clear tipping point in the sharp rise of the top-end market.

Those transfers helped pave the way for subsequent nine-figure deals involving Enzo Fernandez and Moises Caicedo to Chelsea, as well as Declan Rice to Arsenal - all in 2023.

Such deals effectively reinforce one another, made more possible because Premier League clubs are richer and more greatly resourced than ever before.

Broadcast income, sponsorships and commercial revenues continue to dwarf most other European leagues.

Even mid-table Premier League clubs often generate more revenue than Champions League clubs elsewhere in Europe, thus increasing spending power but also strengthening negotiating positions.

Most Premier League clubs are no longer under pressure to sell their best players to balance the books.

The idea that the so-called 'top six' can force sales out of smaller clubs is less applicable in an era of high-wealth owners and greater financial gains, albeit this summer has witnessed somewhat of a resurgence of 'big clubs' raiding 'small clubs'.

Still, the strength of bargaining power has also been leveraged to drive prices higher.

Last summer saw moves for Florian Wirtz (£116.5m) and Alexander Isak (£125m) to Liverpool, while this window has witnessed major sums spent on Elliot Anderson (£116m), Sandro Tonali (£100m), Morgan Rogers (£117m) and Ayyoub Bouaddi (£85.6m).

Those moves have sent top-end averages soaring, up from £38.6m in 2024/25 to £59.8m in 2026/27.

Contextually, Barcelona's £65.4m fee for Rodri is bang on trend for a top-end player in this current market, but his age and remaining contract length would suggest the Spanish club have overpaid against the average.

In short, yes, albeit certain criteria need to be met. The most obvious metric being a Premier League-proven player. Wirtz and Fernandez are the only two exceptions to that rule. Peak age (23-26) is also a major consideration.

Paul Pogba was signed by Man United for £93.25m in 2016 but that transfer, for the time, was a complete anomaly.

The Premier League now has a growing list of deals in the £100m region, despite there being revenue-linked spending rules. Those clubs with huge incomes are still free to invest heavily.

Often, the terms of such deals allow clubs to spread payments over multiple financial years, making the accounting more manageable. And therefore more likely to reoccur.

£100m-plus fees might be the reserve of the Premier League's top clubs for now, but they have become far closer to the norm than the exception.

articles.title: El Manchester City rompe la hucha por Bouaddi para paliar la marcha de Rodri
articles.standfirst: El joven centrocampista francomarroquí deja 100 millones en las arcas del Lille y se convierte en la venta más cara de su historia
articles.summary: El joven centrocampista francomarroquí deja 100 millones en las arcas del Lille y se convierte en la venta más cara de su historia
articles.body: Poco, o prácticamente nada, se va a parecer el centro del campo del Manchester City al que dejó Pep Guardiola tras las salidas de Bernardo Silva y Rodrigo Hernández. Primero, convirtieron a Elliot Anderson en el fichaje más caro de su historia… y acaban de invertir otros 100 millones de euros —95 fijos y cinco en variables— por un Ayyoub Bouaddi (Senlis, 2007) que supera a Nicolas Pepe como la mayor venta del Lille. Firma hasta 2031. "Para mí, el Manchester City es el mejor club del mundo. Es un sueño estar aquí y poder llamarme jugador del City. He dedicado la mayor parte de mi vida a trabajar duro para convertirme en el mejor jugador posible y llegar a la cima del fútbol", fueron las primeras palabras de Bouaddi como nuevo jugador 'cityzen'. Apenas tiene 18 años. Pero se marcha de un Lille que le convirtió en el debutante más joven de su historia —16 años y tres días— con un total de 96 partidos a sus espaldas. Todo un ‘veterano’ que ya se dio a conocer en la Champions 23-24 por sus actuaciones ante Real Madrid, Juventus, Liverpool o Borussia Dortmund. En el estreno ante el Angers con Davide Ancelotti a los mandos, sin embargo, no se vistió de corto y se le vio despidiéndose de los aficionados desplazados al Stade Raymond Kopa. "Con tan solo 18 años, ya posee una inteligencia futbolística excepcional, y eso no hará más que mejorar bajo la tutela de Enzo Maresca", dijo Hugo Viana, director deportivo del Manchester City. Le hemos seguido muy de cerca y, a lo largo de todo este proceso, nos hemos convencido cada vez más de que es un gran talento que triunfará en el City". Su ascenso por las categorías inferiores de la selección francesa fue exponencial… hasta el punto de enfundarse en brazalete de capitán con la Sub21 siendo uno de los jugadores más jóvenes del plantel. Sin embargo, Marruecos levantó el teléfono ofreciéndole la posibilidad de acudir al Mundial 2026 y decidió no esperar a ‘Les Bleus’. "He hecho mi elección y estoy muy orgulloso de ella. Es un alivio haber tomado esta decisión. Estoy muy feliz de representar a mi país, Marruecos. Un gran gracias al pueblo marroquí y espero que logremos cosas bonitas juntos. Mi familia estaba muy contenta", aclaró el propio Bouaddi en la antesala de la Copa del Mundo. Ouahbi lo metió directo al once contra Brasil y firmó un debut para enmarcar en el que mostró su abrumadora personalidad para recibir el balón en primera altura, resistir ante las presiones rivales y darle dinamismo al juego desde el pase. "No me impresionó, porque ya sabía qué tipo de jugador era. La gente se emociona con él. Actuar como lo hizo, a tan corta edad, es genial. Pero recuerda que ha jugado partidos grandes en Champions", decía el seleccionador marroquí. Es cierto que fue de más a menos con el paso del torneo. Pero sus actuaciones fueron lo suficientemente convincentes como para terminar de situarse en el radar de equipos como Real Madrid, PSG o un Manchester City que, aunque tanteó otros nombres como Enzo Fernández o Adam Wharton, ha roto la hucha para fichar al marroquí. En principio, aterriza en el Etihad con el cartel de ser titular en la sala de máquinas junto a Elliot Anderson. Además de Rodri y Bernardo, Reijnders puso rumbo a Al Qadsiah y Nico González está ultimando su marcha al Newcastle. Ante el Bournemouth, incluso, Guéhi arrancó como 'ancla'. La responsabilidad es enorme. Sobre todo, viniendo de donde viene el Manchester City. "Todavía tengo mucho que mejorar", reconoció el propio Bouaddi. Pero, en cada paso que ha dado durante sus primeros años de carrera, siempre ha demostrado que los retos no le quedaban grandes.

articles.title: This day in Juventus history: A new era begins in Turin
articles.summary: Three legendary debuts, two braces, and a 4-0 statement: how Juve rebuilt its spine in a single afternoon.
articles.body:
August 26, 2001, was one of those days where you could feel the tectonic plates of European football shifting in real time.

Juventus were stepping onto the Delle Alpi pitch to open the new Serie A season against Venezia, but all eyes were on the fresh faces in black and white. Zinedine Zidane was gone to Real Madrid , but the massive windfall from that transfer had just built Juve a brand new spine. Lilian Thuram lined up in the backline, Gianluigi Buffon took his spot between the posts, and Pavel Nedvěd trotted out onto the left wing — all three making their official club debuts on the very same afternoon.

From the opening whistle, it didn't feel like a team trying to figure out its new identity; it felt like a machine hitting top gear instantly. Buffon kept a cool, untroubled clean sheet, Thuram pocketed everyone on his side of the pitch, and Nedvěd provided that signature, relentless energy up and down the left flank that Bianconeri fans would come to love for years.

And then there was the attack. Alessandro Del Piero and David Trezeguet turned the afternoon into an absolute exhibition, each bagging a brace in a dominant 4-0 stroll. Trezeguet opened the scoring with a header, Del Piero doubled it literally a minute later, and by the time the final whistle blew, the new-look Juve had made the ultimate opening-day statement.

It was a simple 4-0 win on paper against a side that would end up relegated, but looking back, that afternoon was magic. It was the birth of an iconic era, the first steps of three future legends in Juve shirts, and the launchpad for a season that ended with the Scudetto back where it belonged.

articles.title: Felipe Chávez joins 1. FC Magdeburg on loan
articles.summary: FC Bayern have extended attacker Felipe Chávez’s contract through to 30 June 2028 and agreed a loan move to 1. FC Magdeburg for this season. The 19-year-old...
articles.body:
FC Bayern have extended attacker Felipe Chávez 's contract through to 30 June 2028 and agreed a loan move to 1. FC Magdeburg for this season. The 19-year-old Peru international previously gained Bundesliga experience on loan at 1. FC Köln in the second half of the last campaign.

Christoph Freund , FC Bayern sporting director : "'Pippo' Chávez took the next step in his development with his outings for 1. FC Köln and should now gain more regular playing time at Magdeburg. We have extended his contract because we are convinced of his potential for the future."

The native Bavarian, who was born in Aichach, moved to the FC Bayern Campus from the FC Augsburg academy in summer 2019. He progressed through all the youth teams and after registering four goals and two assists in 19 games for the reserve team, earned his professional debut in the 8-1 win over VfL Wolfsburg at the Allianz Arena in January. He featured seven times in the Bundesliga for Köln. Chávez also made his debut for Peru's senior national team in a friendly against Chile last October.

articles.title: Barcelona cool on Gyokeres: Board doubts stall move as Barca chase striker before deadline
articles.summary: Barcelona are unlikely to make a move for Viktor Gyokeres amid reservations from the club's board over the Arsenal forward.Gyokeres has been linked with a po...
articles.body:
Barcelona are unlikely to make a move for Viktor Gyokeres amid reservations from the club's board over the Arsenal forward.

Gyokeres has been linked with a potential move to Barcelona as the Spanish champions look to sign a centre-forward before the deadline.

The Swedish striker has been shortlisted as an option after frustration in the club's pursuit of Atletico Madrid 's Julian Alvarez .

Atletico are reluctant to sell Alvarez to a La Liga rival, despite the 26-year-old's desire for an exit. Alvarez was jeered by the Atletico supporters at the weekend, after making his first appearance since declaring his wish for a move in the summer.

Gyokeres is viewed as a more attainable option with Arsenal open to a sale for the right price. The 28-year-old scored 21 goals in 55 games last season, but has fallen behind Kai Havertz in the pecking order.

Barca unlikely to bid for Gyokeres; Alvarez stalemate and Lautaro refusal reshape plans

The Athletic are reporting that, despite his impressive goal record, Gyokeres 'is not the most admired name within Barcelona's hierarchy'.

Other options being considered by sporting director Deco include Galatasaray striker Victor Osimhen and Inter Milan captain Lautaro Martinez , though both appear difficult deals.

Inter CEO Guiseppe Marotta said last weekend that Martinez was not for sale under any circumstances. The two-time Serie A leading scorer is believed to be Barca's number-one alternative to Alvarez.

"First and foremost, Lautaro Martinez is our captain and embodies the current history of our club," Marotta told DAZN Italia.

"I can state quite clearly that there is absolutely no chance of him leaving."

articles.title: Preseason Illinois Football Bowl Game Projections
articles.summary: A lot of good destinations for the Illini this December.
articles.body:
Illinois football kicks off its season next Thursday at home against UAB, with hopes that the Illini will once again play in a high-level bowl game following the regular season. Illinois has posted back-to-back nine-win seasons and has played in some of the best Big Ten-affiliated bowl games in three of the last four seasons.

The bowl game streak began in 2022, when Illinois played Mississippi State in the ReliaQuest Bowl in Tampa Bay. The Illini lost that game 19-10, but it was still great to see Illinois playing in one of the best Big Ten-affiliated bowl games. The 2023 season was a down year, with Illinois finishing with just five wins, but the Illini bounced back with back-to-back bowl wins in the Citrus Bowl and Music City Bowl in 2024 and 2025.

Illinois will hope to return to one of those bowl games during the 2026 season. The selection process is not a perfect science, but the final Big Ten standings usually provide a good indication of which bowl game a team could be selected for.

Outside of the College Football Playoff, the best Big Ten team typically plays in the Citrus Bowl in Orlando. That is followed by the ReliaQuest Bowl in Tampa, meaning Illinois has played in two of the conference's best bowl games over the past few seasons.

Here is the ranking of the Big Ten's bowl selections:

Duke's Mayo Bowl vs. ACC (even-numbered years) or Las Vegas Bowl vs. Pac-12/former Pac-12 (odd-numbered years)

Cactus Bowl vs. Big 12 (formerly the Rate Bowl)

As previously mentioned, the selection process is not a perfect science, as bowl officials do not always go strictly by the standings. They try to avoid rematches and prevent schools from playing in the same bowl game too frequently. The Citrus Bowl gets the first pick of the Big Ten teams it would like based on record, fan base, watchability and other factors.

A goal for the Illini should be to remain in the top four bowl games, as they have over the past few seasons. College football insiders have already released their preseason bowl predictions, and there is a wide range of projections for Illinois.

Bryan Fischer, Sports Illustrated: Duke's Mayo Bowl

Pete Fiutak, College Football News: Duke's Mayo Bowl

There is a wide range of projections for the Illini heading into the season. My preseason prediction is that Illinois will play in the Duke's Mayo Bowl in Charlotte. A 7-5 or 8-4 record is usually good enough to earn a bid to that game, and the Illini have never played in the Duke's Mayo Bowl.

Illinois could not be one of the best teams in the Big Ten based on record, but bowl officials also know that Illinois fans will travel to any destination to see their team play.

The College Football Playoff is always the ultimate goal, followed by earning the best bowl bid possible. However, a spot in any of the top four Big Ten-affiliated bowl games would indicate a successful 2026 season for the Illini.

articles.title: Flick talks Alvarez, Balde, Livakovic, Rodri, Lamine, Gavi, Christensen ahead of Barcelona vs Athletic Club
articles.summary: Hansi Flick faced the media ahead of Barcelona’s meeting with Athletic Club, addressing a wide range of issues surrounding his squad as the new season gather...
articles.body:
Hansi Flick faced the media ahead of Barcelona 's meeting with Athletic Club , addressing a wide range of issues surrounding his squad as the new season gathers momentum.

The Barcelona manager was asked about the club's search for a new No. 9, Alejandro Balde 's uncertain role, Dominik Livakovic's arrival and Lamine Yamal 's recent mood.

He also offered updates on Rodri and Gavi while explaining his thinking behind Barcelona's midfield and defensive options.

Barcelona's pursuit of Julian Alvarez continues to dominate discussions around the club, but Flick made it clear that he and sporting director Deco are aligned with Joan Laporta on the matter.

"I think the president was clear, and Deco and I agree with him."

Meanwhile, Balde's future has attracted significant attention in recent weeks, particularly after his reduced role and questions over his place in Flick's plans.

Flick has addressed Alejandro Balde's situation. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

The German coach, though, insisted that the left-back remains part of the squad while making it clear that Balde must continue working to improve.

"He's part of the squad. Whether he plays or not, we'll decide that tomorrow. I've spoken to him; it's important that he's committed to us.

"He's very young and has a lot of potential. He's improved, but he can improve further. He carries the Barça colours in his heart.

"His job is to improve. He has to be 100 per cent committed to professional football and give his all for Barça."

Flick on Livakovic and Barcelona's transfer plans

The manager was also asked about new signing Dominik Livakovic and Barcelona's plans for the goalkeeper position.

"We've discussed the situation. For me, it's good to have experienced goalkeepers for the coming years.

"We're happy with Szczęsny; we'll see what happens in the transfer market. We've got time to make a decision."

On the possibility of further transfers, Flick expressed confidence in his existing squad and praised the work being done by Deco and the club.

"I have complete confidence in my team. We'll certainly need to find solutions for some matches, but the quality we have is immense and that's what we need to make the most of.

"The club and Deco are doing a great job, not just for the present, but for three or four years' time."

Flick explains Lamine's substitution and mood

Flick has also explained Lamine Yamal's mood. (Photo by Daniela Porcelli/Getty Images)

Lamine Yamal's reaction to his recent substitution had generated discussion, but Flick pointed to the youngster's physical preparation and the short time he has had to train following his holiday.

"He's had a few niggles, but we know he's a genius. He had three weeks' holiday and has only been able to train for a few days.

"He couldn't be at his very best – that's only natural. We need to get him back to his best, but I'm grateful that he played 60 minutes for us and was involved in the first two goals.

"That's great, and it also gave us more options for substitutions, so he really contributed a lot to the match. We need him because he's incredible."

Flick was also asked whether Yamal understands why he is being substituted.

"I don't know if he'll understand. It's normal that he wants to play and enjoys playing.

"When you're a champion, you're always going for the next title, because you love winning. That has to be his attitude.

"I can see that all my players have that hunger for a third consecutive league title, and we're ready."

Rodri set for minutes as Flick provides Gavi injury update

Flick confirmed that Rodri is expected to feature against Athletic Club, although the midfielder is unlikely to play a full match.

"Yes, the plan is for him to play for a few minutes."

The Barcelona manager also provided a positive update on Gavi after his recent injury concern.

"He's fine. I think he's doing much better than he was after the match, and from the footage you can see it wasn't that serious. I reckon he might need a week."

Flick also spoke enthusiastically about the possibility of seeing Rodri and Pedri operate together.

"We've also played Bernal, who's similar, but Rodri has more experience; he's a leader. Together with Pedri, they'll allow us to control the match, the ball and the opposition.

"In Elche , in particular, we lost possession too quickly in the first half, and I liked it when Pedri came on because we had more control of the ball and more possession.

"That's what we need. Everyone knows that Rodri is one of the best, and I think we'll enjoy watching them play together at Barça."

Flick pleased with Barcelona's defensive depth

Flick confirms Rodri will play against Athletic Club. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

Finally, Flick was asked about Andreas Christensen and his defensive options, with the manager highlighting the competition available across the back line.

"At the moment, we're in a good position with the players we have in defence, because we've got other options.

"Andreas played very well alongside Gerard, and we've still got Cubarsí, who, in my view, is one of the best centre-backs and played a lot of matches last season.

"So I want to look after him a bit – and our team. He'll want to play, and that's only natural, coming off the back of winning the World Cup and being named the best young player.

"It's incredible to see him play in a World Cup like that, and I'm very pleased to have him," he concluded.

articles.title: ESPN names Wisconsin's Week 1 opponent a college football supervillain
articles.summary: At the historic Lambeau Field, the Wisconsin Badgers will be going head-to-head against the almighty Notre Dame Fighting Irish.
articles.body:
In roughly two weeks, the Wisconsin Badgers will be squaring off in one of the most exciting matchups on the college football calendar.

At the historic Lambeau Field, Luke Fickell 's team will be going head-to-head against the almighty Notre Dame Fighting Irish .

Remember, Notre Dame ended the 2025 campaign on a sour note after opting out of a Bowl game following their 10-2 season, one in which they believe they were robbed of a spot in the College Football Playoffs.

Recently, the Fighting Irish were listed as one of college football's greatest supervillains by ESPN's Ryan McGee.

"From their continued life as a nonconference football independent that still plays sort of an ACC schedule to having their own personal television contract for the last few decades and their continued status as a lone wolf in the College Football Playoff selection room, Notre Dame has long wielded exclusive powers. And as much as the Irish's fanbase has relished the role, all other fanbases hate them for it," writes McGee.

On September 6 at 7:30 p.m. ET, the Badgers will have the rare chance to take down the Fighting Irish, a team that opens the year ranked No. 4 in the preseason AP Poll .

articles.title: Former CSU football star helps Italy make LA28 in new Olympic sport
articles.summary: Former CSU safety Henry Blackburn helped Italy qualify for the 2028 Olympics in flag football, putting the ex-Ram one step closer to competing in LA.
articles.body:
A former Colorado State football player could be participating in the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles.

But wait, tackle football isn't in the Olympics? No, but flag football now is.

The Summer Games have added flag football as a sport for LA28 and former Ram safety Henry Blackburn has helped Italy qualify.

Italy took silver in the 2026 IFAF Flag Football World Championships earlier in August and a 41-36 win over Canada in the semifinals secured a spot at the Olympics.

"See you soon LA28," Blackburn posted on Instagram after Italy qualified.

Blackburn is from Colorado and grew up in Boulder, but holds an Italian passport.

Blackburn was a safety for the Rams from 2020-24 where he twice served as a captain. He had 272 career tackles at CSU with 9.5 tackles-for-loss, four sacks, five interceptions, five fumble recoveries and three fumbles forced.

Blackburn plays tackle football for the Ancona Dolphins in the Italian Football League.

Sports reporter Kevin Lytle can be found on social media on X , Instagram and Threads @Kevin_Lytle and on Bluesky .

images.caption: Italy players pose for a photograph as they celebrate following the team's victory in the semifinal match between Canada and Italy and a ticket to the Olympics Games on day three of the IFAF World Flag Düsseldorf 2026 on August 15, 2026 in Duesseldorf, Germany.

articles.title: Ayyoub Bouaddi: Manchester City sign Morocco midfielder from Lille in Â£86m deal
articles.summary: Manchester City complete the signing of Morocco midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille in a Â£85.6m deal on a five-year contract.
articles.body:
Manchester City have signed Morocco midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille in a Â£85.6m deal.

The 18-year-old joins on a five-year contract, subject to international clearance, with City paying Â£81.4m upfront plus Â£4.2m in add-ons.

Enzo Maresca's side moved to sign Bouaddi after selling central midfielders Rodri to Barcelona in a Â£65m deal and Tijjani Reinders to Al-Qadsiah for Â£52m.

He impressed at this summer's World Cup - starting five of Morocco's six matches in their run to the quarter-finals - after becoming a key member of Lille's side in Ligue 1.

"This is a very special day for me and my family. Manchester City are, for me, the best club in the world. It's a dream to be here and be able to call myself a City player," said Bouaddi.

"I have spent most of my life working hard to become the best player I can be and reach the top of the game.

"I've watched City for many years, and I love their style of play. City always try and play quality football. And they have shown they are winners - this club feels like it's built to win."

Bouaddi made 96 appearances for Lille after making his debut in 2023, helping them finish third in Ligue 1 last season.

At the age of 16 he became the youngest footballer to ever play for the French side on his senior debut against Faroese club KI in the Europa League, before announcing himself on the world stage by playing a starring role in Lille's Champions League victory over Real Madrid in 2024.

Bouaddi will form part of a revamped midfield, with City already bringing in England midfielder Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest for Â£116m.

Bouaddi functions as a deep-lying conductor and would complement Anderson, who is comfortable as a box-to-box midfielder as well as the number six role he plays for England.

City are also set to make an offer for Chelsea 's Argentina midfielder Enzo Fernandez but it remains to be seen whether a deal can be struck with the 25-year-old valued at Â£120m.

Bouaddi's signing comes after Brazilian winger Savinho, now known as Savio, joined Tottenham in a Â£75m deal earlier this week.

Spurs have also agreed a loan deal to sign City's Egypt forward Omar Marmoush, while Spain midfielder Nico Gonzalez is set to leave Maresca's side to join Newcastle in a Â£52m deal.

Man City to make offer for Â£120m-rated Fernandez Published 1 hour ago

Man City to make offer for Â£120m-rated Fernandez

Tottenham agree loan for Man City's Marmoush Published 2 hours ago

Tottenham agree loan for Man City's Marmoush

Analysis - Midfield rebuild taking shape

City's midfield transformation continues to take shape with the acquisition of teenage star Bouaddi, who will play alongside club-record signing Anderson.

At just 18, Bouaddi has big boots to fill following the departure of 2024 Ballon d'Or winner Rodri, who became one of the best midfielders in the world at City and departed for Barcelona last week.

The Spaniard, Reijnders and Bernardo Silva have all left from City's midfield this summer and Nico Gonzalez is also set to make an exit after Newcastle agreed a Â£52m deal for the player.

It means Maresca still needs reinforcements in the middle of the park and City will make an offer for Chelsea 's Â£120m-rated midfielder Enzo Fernandez to bolster ranks - whether they can match the asking price and get the deal done before Tuesday's deadline remains to be seen.

There has been significant change in the City squad this summer and with the season already under way Anderson, Bouaddi and possibly Fernandez will all need to hit the ground running.

articles.title: How far does Joel Klatt have Notre Dame going through the CFP?
articles.summary: Notre Dame was snubbed out of last season's College Football Playoff. Joel Klatt has the Irish reaching it this year, but will they win it all?
articles.body:
Fox Sports college football analyst Joel Klatt recently announced his predictions for the 2027 College Football Playoff .

Much like other CFP predictions for the upcoming season , Klatt has Notre Dame reaching the national championship game. Going into the CFP as the second seed, Klatt has the Irish winning it all for the first time in nearly 40 years.

Through Fox Sports' The Joel Klatt Show podcast, Klatt predicted that Notre Dame will beat seventh-seeded Georgia in the quarterfinals, defeat third-seeded Miami in the semifinals then knock off top-seeded Oregon in the title game.

It remains to be seen how Notre Dame will respond this season after being snubbed out of the CFP last year. However, with a stacked roster this season, the Irish are poised for redemption and to raise the CFP trophy.

The Irish will begin their run to the national championship game at home on Sept. 6 against Wisconsin.

articles.title: Joe Rodon: The unity in the squad is unbelievable
articles.summary: Leeds United made it back-to-back victories to begin the 2026/27 campaign, both of which came at the City Ground against Nottingham Forest.Following on from...
articles.body:
Leeds United made it back-to-back victories to begin the 2026/27 campaign, both of which came at the City Ground against Nottingham Forest .

Following on from the Premier League success at the weekend, Daniel Farke's side produced another solid display to progress into the next round of the Carabao Cup.

Speaking to ITV straight after the game, defender Joe Rodon gave his thoughts on another impressive away victory for his side.

"We know it's a difficult place to come, but overall very happy to keep a clean sheet and win the game," Rodon reflected.

The opening goal came from fellow Wales international Daniel James and our number 6 was pleased to see his national side and club teammate get off the mark for the season, as well as praising the rest of the squad.

"We all know what he's capable of. I'm over the moon for him tonight, and he showed his quality, and it was a great finish.

"We need everyone. You know, we've got a very good squad, and it's a long season, so the unity in the squad is unbelievable, and that's why we need everyone together.

"We want to change the mentality. We want to grow again as a group, and we want to go into every game trying to win.

"The new signings have been top, they've gelled in really well. We want to continue this momentum and go to next weekend."

Manchester City have completed the £85.6 million ($116.6 million) signing of Lille midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi , the Premier League club have announced.

The 18-year-old Morocco international has signed a five-year contract at the Etihad Stadium after the clubs agreed a fee over the weekend.

The Press Association understands the deal is worth an initial £81 million with the rest of the fee made up in potential add-ons.

Bouaddi's arrival increases manager Enzo Maresca's midfield options following the recent departures of Rodri and Tijjani Reijnders , with Nico Gonzalez also poised to leave.

He is City's second major summer signing after the £116 million capture of Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest .

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo: Ten-man Al-Nassr seal dramatic win after Portugal star subbed off
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo is taken off at half-time with his 10-man Al-Nassr side 2-0 down - but they fight back to seal a dramatic win over Al-Ettifaq.
articles.body:
Cristiano Ronaldo was taken off at half-time with his 10-man Al-Nassr side 2-0 down - before they fought back to seal a dramatic win over Al-Ettifaq.

Defending Saudi Pro League champions Al-Nassr got off to a dreadful start on Tuesday when goalkeeper Bento was sent off after just 12 minutes and they were two goals behind at the break.

Ronaldo, 41, making his first start since the World Cup, left the pitch in frustration at half-time and was then substituted by manager Ange Postecoglou.

But Postecoglou's decisions proved to be vindicated with Al-Nassr launching a second-half comeback.

Sadio Mane and Abdulelah Al Amri scored inside three minutes to draw Al-Nassr level with 13 minutes to go, before former Liverpool forward Mane got the winner in added time.

The win helped Al-Nassr go top of the table after three straight victories this season.

Former Tottenham and Nottingham Forest boss Postegoclou said Ronaldo, who spread his arms in a questioning gesture towards the bench when he was substituted, was taken off as part of a different tactical approach.

"When I made the substitutions, including taking Ronaldo off, I believed the players coming on could make an impact," Postecoglou said.

"I came here to help the players, so as I said, I'm proud of them because every substitute made a positive contribution.

"I'm here to help the team with what I see, and everyone knows that Ronaldo hasn't played in a long time. He performed exceptionally well in the first half, and we opted for a different approach."

Postecoglou took over at Al-Nassr last month after being sacked by Forest last October following just 39 days in charge.

Five-time Ballon d'Or winner Ronaldo married his partner Georgina Rodriguez earlier this month and has said this is likely to be his last season as a player so he can focus more on his family.

articles.body:
Celta Vigo are reportedly "closing in on [a] personal terms agreement" with Stefan Bajcetic .

Fabrizio Romano shared the update on X (formerly Twitter) on Wednesday morning, with the midfielder looking unlikely to resurrect his Liverpool career.

The Spaniard's current terms are set to expire in the summer of 2027.

Stefan Bajcetic could leave Liverpool this summer

(Photo by Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images)

According to recent reports, the footballer is understood to have flown to Finland for fitness checks ahead of a mooted switch to La Liga.

It's suggested that Bajcetic would have to terminate his contract a year early for the deal to go through. However, it's hard to imagine Liverpool standing in the player's way, given his current value will more than likely be minimal following a string of injury issues and mixed loan spells.

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

More to the point, it's not an option we can seriously rely upon in midfield, so we've no doubt Andoni Iraola would be prepared to sanction the exit.

Lots of exit activity but Liverpool are desperate for incomings

For a footballer who arrived with plenty of potential, and even briefly threatened to show promise of becoming a mainstay under Jurgen Klopp, it's a massive shame to see the former Las Palmas loanee's Anfield career fizzle out so disappointingly.

Yet it underlines the fact that Liverpool are proving to be frustratingly quiet on the incomings front, while further thinning their squad.

We've already seen Curtis Jones make a permanent switch to Inter Milan , and the club is adamant that we won't be signing any midfielders in the window .

Yet, in the one department where we should be seeing progress, we've seen talks stall for Yankuba Minteh and Liverpool step away from a deal with PSG for Ibrahim Mbaye .

articles.title: Maryland field hockey 2026 season preview
articles.summary: The Terps look to rebound after a rocky 2025 season and return toward the pinnacle of the sport.
articles.body:
No. 13 Maryland field hockey has had plenty of incredible seasons throughout its illustrious history.

Last year, the Terps entered the season ranked fourth in the National Field Hockey Coaches Association Poll, but they only managed 10 wins, the second-fewest in the Missy Meharg era. In postseason play, the Terps dropped a must-win game to Ohio State in the Big Ten Tournament quarterfinals and failed to qualify for the NCAA Tournament for only the fourth time since Meharg became head coach in 1988.

Now, with the disappointing campaign behind them, the Terps have shifted their sights to 2026 in an effort to reassume their position at the top of the Big Ten.

While the Terps retained most of their top players during the offseason, they still lost plenty of talent, as 12 of the 26 players from last season exited the program. Arguably the two biggest losses are on defense, as both Ericka Morris-Adams and Fleur Knopert graduated. The pair headlined a defense that conceded just 19 goals last season, fourth-fewest in the NCAA.

Morris-Adams was a four-year Terp who played in 83 games and started 64 during her time in College Park. She was a captain for last year's team.

Knopert, on the other hand, spent just two seasons at Maryland after transferring from Ball State, but she produced a pair of strong campaigns and made a seamless transition from forward to defender last offseason. She logged 901 minutes in 2025, third-most on the squad.

In the midfield, the biggest missing piece is Annemijn Klijnhout. In her two years with the Terps, Klijnhout started all 38 games she played and accumulated 12 points. Additionally, she received All-Big Ten First Team honors in 2025.

In the forward department, the Terps lost Ella Gaitan to conference foe Penn State. Gaitan was one of the Terps' top offensive threats a year ago, scoring five goals and adding an assist. For an offense that finished last season at the bottom of the Big Ten in goalscoring, her presence will be missed.

Despite the many absences, the Terps still bring back a lot of contributors, and goalkeeper Alyssa Klebasko is at the top of that list. The senior brings a veteran presence, having started 53 games in her career. In 2025, she finished second in the conference with 1.07 goals allowed and tied a career-high with six shutouts.

The defense is anchored by another senior in Josie Hollamon. The only upperclassman of the unit, Hollamon has started every game for the Terps through the first three years of her career and has racked up the accolades. She's a two-time all-Big Ten first team selection and was named a second-team All-American by the NFHCA in 2025. She can also produce on the offensive side, as she's totaled 14 goals and 11 assists for her career. A captain for last year's group, Hollamon is expected to continue in a similar leadership position this year, especially with an underclassmen-heavy squad.

A trio of international stars make up the midfield. Junior Ella Fehr — a native of Berlin, Germany — returns for her second year in College Park after transferring from VCU. She started all 18 games last year and is set for an even larger role this year.

Sophomore Feliz Kuhne is also set for an expanded role in her second season with the Terps. A native of the Netherlands, Kuhne played in the Hoofdklasse, the Netherlands' top division of professional field hockey, prior to her arrival in the United States.

The Australian Maia Adamson rounds out the group. She started all 18 games as a freshman last year and was named to the Big Ten's All-Freshman team. In Maryland's lone postseason game, she registered the tying goal in what was ultimately a 2-1 defeat.

Up front, Maci Bradford and Jordyn Hollamon lead the charge. Bradford, another experienced senior, topped the Terps in both assists and points last season, earning her all-Big Ten second team honors. Her cousin, Jordyn Hollamon, was just as impressive, winning Big Ten Freshman of the Year with a team-high seven goals. She also attempted a team-high 54 shots, more than double the next-highest total.

To fill out the remaining roster spots, Meharg utilized the transfer portal and tapped into the high school ranks.

From the portal, the 39th-year head coach grabbed senior midfielder Rachael Whitehead and junior midfielder Francisca Eschoyez. Whitehead – a three-year starter at Delaware – was selected to the All-MPSF Team last season and has tallied 24 career points.

Eschoyez is arguably Meharg's best get of the offseason. In 2025, the Italian led Quinnipiac in every major offensive category and took home Big East Offensive Player of the Year, All-Big East and NFHCA third team All-American honors. She comes to Maryland with 55 career points and should boost an offense that struggled mightily last year.

On the high school side, Meharg struck gold once again — she landed a top-three domestic recruiting class, according to Max Field Hockey, for the second straight year. This year's class is headlined by a pair of Max Field Hockey top-10 prospects in Ella Beach and Aida Ierubino.

Beach, a native of Northbrook, Illinois, was a three-time All-State selection and a 2025 All-American in high school. She comes from a family full of Terps, as her mother played field hockey and her father played soccer for Maryland.

Ierubino, from Doylestown, Pennsylvania, was a two-time first team All-American and a four-time first team All-State selection prior to her arrival in College Park. In addition, she was part of this year's USA U18 Women's National Team.

To complete the roster, Meharg added Babs van Hest, a junior forward from the Netherlands. Similar to Kuhne, van Hest played in the Hoofdklasse before joining the Terps.

The path to success will not be easy this autumn, as the Terps face seven tournament teams from a year ago – including both national finalists.

Maryland kicks off the season by hosting the Conference Cup, featuring Drexel, James Madison and Temple. The Terps will play Drexel on Aug. 28 and Temple two days later.

The first big test comes the following weekend, as the Terps travel to Massachusetts for the B1G/ACC Challenge. Maryland will once again face Boston College and Duke – both of whom toppled the Terps last year.

The rest of the non-conference schedule is littered with quality opponents. At home, the Terps will play St. Joseph's on Sept. 13 and Wake Forest on Sept. 20. On the road, Maryland will match up with Princeton — 2025's national runner-up — on Sept. 29.

Big Ten play will yet again be a grind. Six of the conference's nine teams finished .500 or better in 2025.

After a non-conference matchup with Delaware kicks off October, the Terps will travel to Ann Arbor to face off with Michigan. Upon returning to College Park, the Terps will host a pair of games against Michigan State and Ohio State on Oct. 16 and 18, respectively. In the latter contest, the Terps will hope to avenge their postseason loss to the Buckeyes from a year ago.

Then, it's back on the road for arguably the toughest opponent this season: Northwestern. Maryland will face the two-time reigning national champions on Oct. 22 in Evanston.

The regular season concludes with one more important showdown, as the Terps welcome Iowa on Oct. 30 for Senior Day.

It's been a while since the Terps took home some hardware — they haven't won a Big Ten Tournament title since 2018, and they haven't been crowned national champions since 2011. It won't get any easier this season, but the Terps are confident that a mix of veteran leadership and exciting young talent will put them back in contention. After all, as long as Meharg is still head coach, a title run is always in the cards.

articles.title: Barcelona midfielder set to miss Athletic Club clash after missing final training session
articles.summary: Barcelona’s final preparations for their La Liga meeting with Athletic Club brought contrasting news from the training ground, with Gavi working away from th...
articles.body:
Barcelona 's final preparations for their La Liga meeting with Athletic Club brought contrasting news from the training ground, with Gavi working away from the group while Rodri continued his return to full first-team activity.

According to Mundo Deportivo , Barcelona completed another session on Wednesday as Hansi Flick's side prepared for their league debut at the Spotify Camp Nou.

Gavi was the notable absentee from the main group, with the midfielder continuing to recover after suffering a contusion.

His absence makes his involvement against Athletic Club highly unlikely, even though Flick offered a reassuring update on the player's condition ahead of the match.

Gavi unlikely to feature against Athletic Club

Gavi has become one of the main concerns for Flick in the build-up to Thursday's game after failing to train with his teammates.

The Barcelona midfielder worked separately as the coaching staff continued to manage his recovery.

Gavi did not train with the group. (Photo by Francisco Macia/Getty Images)

While the situation does not appear to be serious , the lack of group training so close to the match means he is unlikely to be involved against Athletic Club.

Flick had already sought to calm concerns when discussing the midfielder's fitness.

"He's fine. I think he's doing much better than he was after the match, and from the footage you can see it wasn't that serious.

The coach's assessment suggests that Barcelona are unlikely to take any unnecessary risks with Gavi, particularly at this early stage of the season.

While Gavi's situation remains a concern, Barcelona received more encouraging news regarding Rodri.

Rodri will make his Barcelona debut vs Athletic Club. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

The summer signing completed another full training session with the first-team group, continuing the process of reintegration after returning to normal team activities in recent sessions.

Rodri now appears ready to make his long-awaited Barcelona debut.

Flick has confirmed that the midfielder is part of the plan for the Athletic Club match, although his involvement is expected to be limited.

"Yes, the plan is for him to play for a few minutes."

Those minutes could give Barcelona fans their first opportunity to see the club's blockbuster signing in competitive action.

articles.title: Celtic count the cost of Champions League flop
articles.summary: Scottish champions Celtic face a second successive season without Champions League football, a blow which will not only have serious financial consequences,...
articles.body:
Scottish champions Celtic face a second successive season without Champions League football, a blow which will not only have serious financial consequences, manager Martin O'Neill admitted, but could also deter players from signing for them.

Having gone out to unheralded Kazakh side Kairat Almaty in last year's play-offs, Celtic suffered an even greater humiliation on Tuesday, squandering a four-goal aggregate lead against Austrian champions LASK to lose 5-1 on the night and 5-4 overall.

Their failure to reach the league phase will cost them an estimated £40 million ($55 million), even with the consolation of competing in the second-tier Europa League.

O'Neill, who in his second full-time spell at the historic club, had guided them to the title on the final day of the season with a dramatic win over rivals Hearts, said missing out was costly in every respect.

"The qualification for the Champions League is major, it's major in every aspect," said the 74-year-old Northern Irishman.

"Financially, for prestige, but we have to pick ourselves up. That's my responsibility again to do that.

"I think I said last week that if you could qualify for the Champions League there would be players wanting to come on that basis.

O'Neill, who won the European Cup twice as a player with Nottingham Forest , admitted the squad needed strengthening as the performance had underlined their weaknesses.

"We know that we are a million miles from the finished article," said O'Neill, who in his first spell took Celtic to the 2003 UEFA Cup final.

"That's absolutely true. I think we thought that anyway."

O'Neill, who missed the start of the domestic season because he underwent a procedure in hospital for a "couple of ailments rolled into one", was more diplomatic in his analysis than club captain Callum McGregor .

The 33-year-old midfielder, who has spent his entire career at Celtic aside from a loan spell early on at English side Notts County, did not hold back.

"We got what we deserved," he told Amazon Prime.

"We were passive all night. We looked scared to go and win the game.

"I didn't think we were that good in the first leg either. We scored at good times and got away with it.

"We have to suck it up. We apologise to our supporters and the club because there's no way we should lose that game."

Although O'Neill said he assumed full "responsibility" for the cataclysmic performance, McGregor believed the blame lay elsewhere.

"It's as much on the players as everyone else. You can't look for excuses elsewhere," he said.

"You'll now see what people are made of. When you play like that you can't have any excuses whatsoever.

"When you go 1-0 up in the game and it still doesn't settle you, that is on us."

McGregor said the character of the players would be tested now.

"You fall at a big hurdle and these questions are going to be asked. You can't lose by that margin then look for excuses elsewhere," he said.

"You have to bounce back, you have to show a reaction and that's what Celtic are all about."

The players' first opportunity to rebound comes on Saturday when the Premiership table-toppers -- they have six points after two matches -- host Falkirk, who have just one point.

articles.body:
Rômulo (24) missed RB Leipzig 's DFB Pokal victory over Eintracht Trier, and now the Brazilian attacker could miss their Bundesliga opening against Borussia Mönchengladbach.

The Saxony club confirmed that due to tendon irritation in his knee, Rômulo was not able to partake in team training as Martin Demichelis prepares for his first Bundesliga game in charge of the Saxony club.

Additionally, Ørjan Nyland (minor foot issue), Assan Ouédraogo (shoulder) and Christoph Baumgartner (rehab) didn't participate in team training.

Because of Rômulo's absence, it could mean that young French attacker Tidiam Gomis (20) could retain his place as Leipzig's focal point in attack. The former Caen player played only 337 minutes across 18 Bundesliga games in 2025/26, and returned one goal.

The loss of Rômulo – who scored nine goals and provided four assists in 30 Bundesliga games last term – is obviously a big one. There's also a chance that Christopher Nkunku , having returning on loan from Milan , could feature for the Red Bulls.

articles.title: Vuelven las Ventanas FIBA... y la lluvia de pasaportes
articles.standfirst: Con los partidos de selecciones, nuevos jugadores estadounidenses pasarán a ser comunitarios: Kobi Simmons, Damion Baugh, Moses Wright...
articles.summary: Con los partidos de selecciones, nuevos jugadores estadounidenses pasarán a ser comunitarios: Kobi Simmons, Damion Baugh, Moses Wright...
articles.body: Cada Ventana FIBA se ha convertido en una oportunidad para que jugadores estadounidenses consigan un nuevo pasaporte y pasen a gozar de la condición de comunitarios. En una competición como la Euroliga, donde no hay límite de extracomunitarios, es un detalle insignificante, pero sí en Ligas nacionales o competiciones FIBA, donde existen cupos. Aprovechando las Ventanas que arrancan esta semana, los baskonistas Kobi Simmons y Damion Baugh tendrán su documentación. El primero está en la preselección de Costa de Marfil y el segundo, en la de Congo. Moses Wright, fichaje interruptus del Barcelona y ahora en el Armani Milán, estará con Macedonia del Norte. Ninguno de ellos tiene vinculación con esos países pero conseguirán la nacionalidad en cuanto salten a la pista. Se trata de un requisito exigido por FIBA que hace años que ha quedado obsoleto. Se permitió la presencia de un nacionalizado por selección y torneo con la intención de aumentar la capacidad deportiva de países pequeños o con escaso potencial. Sin embargo, la norma se ha pervertido tanto que ahora cada Ventana parece un trapicheo. Pocas Federaciones son las que evitan estas nacionalizaciones exprés. España, por ejemplo, lo hizo con Lorenzo Brown. Sin embargo, el caso más extremo es el de la mencionada Macedonia del Norte. Moses Wright será el sexto jugador al que dan el pasaporte en el último año. Parece que les cuesta dar con el nacionalizado que mejor encaje en su selección. Antes que el pívot se han puesta esa camiseta recientemente Jacob Wiley, Omari Moore, Ethan Happ, DJ Stewart y Nate Sestina. Todos han jugado o jugarán en la Liga Endesa, donde se necesitan cuatro cupos en convocatorias de 12 jugadores. Esos nuevos pasaportes abren puertas. Pero no parece que nacionalizar en masa le haya dado buenos resultados al combinado macedonio. Está intentando ganarse un hueco en el Eurobasket de 2029, no alcanza la cita continental desde hace 11 años y, por supuesto, no ha conseguido meterse en la pelea por estar en la Copa del Mundo de 2027. El tránsito de pasaportes es tan habitual que los jugadores hablan abiertamente de ello. Jarred Vanderbilt, alero de los Lakers que está de campus de entrenamiento con el equipo en Eslovenia ha asegurado que no le importaría conseguir la nacionalidad. No sería el primer compañero que Luka Doncic capta para la selección. Antes lo hizo con Anthony Randolph y Jaxson Hayes. Mike Tobey y Josh Nebo también tiene pasaporte esloveno.

articles.title: Bigas pide un Elche unido y convencido para buscar los tres puntos en Santander
articles.standfirst: El central franjiverde ha dejado claro que si plasman lo que están trabajando tienen muchas opciones de llevarse los tres puntos
articles.summary: El central franjiverde ha dejado claro que si plasman lo que están trabajando tienen muchas opciones de llevarse los tres puntos
articles.body: Pedro Bigas, uno de los capitanes del Elche, ha comparecido este miércoles ante los medios en la previa del partido que el conjunto ilicitano disputará este viernes, a las 19:00 horas, frente al Racing de Santander en El Sardinero, correspondiente a la tercera jornada de Primera División. El central ha reivindicado la confianza del equipo tras la derrota ante el Barcelona y ha destacado la importancia de mantener la unión para afrontar el encuentro. Bigas considera que el 0-5 ante el Barça dejó aspectos positivos pese a lo abultado del marcador: “Se hizo una buena primera parte. Con estos equipos, al mínimo despiste te castigan”, ha señalado. El capitán franjiverde entiende que el resultado fue “excesivo”, aunque reconoce que durante algunos tramos de la segunda mitad el equipo perdió concentración. “No fuimos del todo un equipo, con tramos en los que estuvimos más despistados. Que nos sirva de aprendizaje”, ha explicado. El defensa también ha valorado el respaldo de la afición, que continúa mostrando su apoyo pese a la goleada encajada: “A nadie le gusta que le goleen”, ha admitido, antes de remarcar que el vestuario no tiene dudas sobre el compromiso de la grada. “Solo nos piden que nos esforcemos y lo estamos haciendo. Tampoco creo que haya hecho daño la derrota contra el Barça. Estamos con confianza, que es lo importante”, ha afirmado. El encuentro ante el Barcelona supuso además los primeros minutos de Bigas esta temporada. El jugador ha reconocido que su pretemporada fue diferente debido a unas molestias en la rodilla, aunque asegura encontrarse bien. “Quería llegar bien al arranque de Liga. Tengo que ponerle las cosas difíciles al entrenador y él decidirá. Seguir trabajando y entrenando para tener minutos”, ha apuntado. De cara al duelo en Santander, Bigas ha insistido en la necesidad de que el Elche mantenga la cohesión durante los 90 minutos: “Lo primero es estar convencidos y lo estamos. Tenemos que ir allí unidos en todo momento, que el equipo no se parta”, ha explicado. En este sentido, considera que el trabajo realizado durante la semana ofrece motivos para el optimismo: “Si hacemos las cosas como estamos trabajando tenemos grandes opciones”. El capitán también ha pedido fortaleza mental ante cualquier escenario que pueda plantear el partido: “Si en cualquier momento nos ponemos en contra en el marcador, que no nos desanime”, ha señalado. A su juicio, el Elche tendrá opciones de regresar con los tres puntos si mantiene su plan de juego: “Haciendo las cosas bien tenemos una buena oportunidad para llevarnos los tres puntos”. Sobre el cierre del mercado, que afronta sus últimos seis días, Bigas ha evitado pronunciarse de forma categórica sobre la composición definitiva de la plantilla: “Nunca se sabe. Sabemos cómo trabajan aquí”, ha comentado. El defensa considera que los fichajes todavía necesitan un periodo de adaptación, pero confía en el potencial del grupo: “Tenemos buen equipo. Poniendo a todos al 100% tiene potencial”. Eso sí, ha dejado clara su preferencia: “Si tiene que llegar alguien, bienvenido sea; esperemos que no haya salidas”. Uno de los nombres propios de la actualidad del Elche es el de David Affengruber, cuya continuidad sigue estando en el aire tras recibir numerosas ofertas de equipos importantes. Bigas no ha ocultado su deseo de que el central permanezca en el equipo: “Me encantaría. Lo que pase no lo sabemos. Si fuese decisión mía, lo renovaría”, ha afirmado. El capitán ha destacado la trayectoria del futbolista y ha reconocido que su situación puede despertar el interés de otros clubes: “Para otros clubes es una tentación, basta con ver la carrera que está haciendo”. Affengruber tiene contrato, pero Bigas admite que la decisión final no depende del vestuario: “Si podemos hacer algo, lo haremos para que se quede”. Más allá de los aspectos estrictamente futbolísticos, Bigas ha destacado el ambiente dentro del vestuario como una de las principales fortalezas del Elche: “El día a día es muy bueno”, ha asegurado. “Somos una familia y el Elche se caracteriza por eso. Viene gente muy sana y eso no tiene que perderse nunca porque, a la larga, nos hace sacar más rendimiento”. Por último, el capitán ha realizado una valoración positiva del arranque de temporada pese a la derrota ante el Barcelona. Ha recordado que el equipo terminó invicto la pretemporada y considera que el partido contra el Deportivo dejó buenas sensaciones. Frente al Barça, destaca especialmente la primera mitad, en la que el Elche “les competimos de tú a tú”. Sin embargo, también ha subrayado la enorme dificultad de la Primera División: “Es muy difícil sacar resultados”.

articles.title: 2026 Week 0 College Football Predictions for Every Game
articles.summary: After a not-so-patient seven months of waiting, college football is back. The offseason is, almost officially, over.
articles.body:
After a not-so-patient seven months of waiting, college football is back. The offseason is, almost officially, over.

Once again, the campaign will formally kick off overseas. Dublin, Ireland is playing host to a clash between North Carolina and TCU, the latter of which cruised to a blowout win in last season's matchup.

Even though Week 0 includes a modest eight contests, the storylines are plentiful.

There's a league showdown in the ACC, while FBS newcomers North Dakota State and Sacramento State are both making their top-level debuts. A ranked USC team is in action, and a huge Group of 6 game closes the opening slate.

When: Noon ET on ESPN (in Dublin, Ireland)

Last year, the much-anticipated debut of Bill Belichick ended with TCU straight-up steamrolling North Carolina. TCU scored two defensive touchdowns and amassed 542 yards compared to UNC's 222.

Is that going to happen again? I mean, obviously not.

Optimism isn't exactly in rich supply for UNC, although its defense should at least be competent again. The greater issue is whether former Maryland and Wisconsin QB Billy Edwards Jr. can elevate an anemic offense.

Maybe that happens. But I will unapologetically sit in the "believe it when I see it" camp for UNC opposite a pesky TCU defense.

Initially scheduled as a nonconference affair and previously set to be played in Brazil, this is now an ACC matchup at Virginia.

Because of the switch, though, there are greater stakes here compared to last year. North Carolina State won 35-31, but it wasn't a league tilt—and UVA eventually stood atop the ACC standings at the end of the regular season.

NC State signal-caller CJ Bailey is back, and he's talented enough to take control of the game at his best. Still, the blend of UVA's veteran offensive line and deep group of returning players on defense is tough to pick against at home.

By the time December rolls around, we might be talking about this very result between Memphis and UNLV.

This season, the highest-ranked Group of Six team—not necessarily the highest-ranked G6 champion—will be included in the College Football Playoff. These two programs are among the more notable early contenders.

In short: Don't underestimate the value of this outcome.

The major challenge with Memphis is that new coach Charles Huff overhauled the team, adding more than 70 players to the roster. We all have opinions about the Tigers, but that amount of transition means it's a huge guess.

So, hey, if you believe they'll excel immediately, I can't prove the opposite. I'm a long-term believer in Huff's upside at Memphis, too.

This early, however, I'll trust Jackson Arnold—the former QB at Oklahoma and Auburn—to propel a more cohesive UNLV team playing in its own building.

articles.title: Expert College Football Betting Locks for 2026 Games of the Year
articles.summary: If you have a hunch or a feeling or an opinion, now is your time. A season of college football betting is at your fingertips.
articles.body:
If you have a hunch or a feeling or an opinion, now is your time. A season of college football betting is at your fingertips.

There's no longer a need to wait. Many of the season's biggest games have point spreads already, based on where expectations sit before the games begin.

Reaching these spreads given the current climate is no easy assignment. With so much movement across the sport—with rosters being built year over year—finding an edge is harder than it has ever been.

Then again, a good edge can be had. If you feel strongly about a certain team, that feeling can give you an edge that will soon fade if and when that team finds success.

Or you can pick your spots, look for value and invest before it all begins. That's exactly what the plan is here.

We're scouting college football's entire slate of games in search of winners—a preview of the weekly ritual that will take place all season on Bleacher Report.

Here are our picks for some of the biggest games of the year.

September 12: Michigan (-1.5) vs. Oklahoma

The first true test of the Kyle Whittingham era will come during Week 2. While this is not a conference game, the impact for both College Football Playoff hopefuls is seismic.

This is, quite simply, a bet on Whittingham and his ability to coach a football program still ripe with talent. It's a bet on sophomore QB Bryce Underwood, too. Oh, and new offensive coordinator Jason Beck. Look for him to work absolute wonders.

That's not to say Brent Venables isn't capable of winning this game. The Sooners did a brilliant job navigating a challenging schedule last year, which included an 11-point home win over the Wolverines.

Switching venues, however, should swing momentum significantly. And while a healthy (and swole) John Mateer is intriguing, there is something about this Oklahoma team that I can't fully trust.

It won't be pretty or easy. In fact, it'll look and feel very Utah-esque. But Michigan finds a way to win a close, ugly football game.

While the Iron Bowl and Ohio State-Michigan typically provide the most hatred on the football schedule, this game is positioned to break that mold.

We know the story and the drama. Lane Kiffin coached Ole Miss, bringing the program to new heights. In the heart of a CFB Playoff run, he left the Rebels high and dry to coach LSU—a move whose fallout lingered longer than it should have.

Ole Miss made a run, LSU put together a solid roster and the two will meet nine months later in a game that will ooze venom. Given recent headlines, perhaps it's still coming together.

Oh, and the game will be played in Oxford. That part is important.

To be clear, Trinidad Chambliss is one of the most exciting players in all of football. And Ole Miss did well to keep pieces around him.

But we still don't exactly know what a Pete Golding-coached team will look like with the euphoria and charm of a playoff berth gone. Plus, for all the drama and headlines that come with Kiffin, he knows how to build a roster.

Putting QB Sam Leavitt squarely at the center of the additions was obviously the biggest enhancement. But additions on both the offensive and defensive lines were also noteworthy.

It won't be perfect, although the shift will be on display right away. Despite all the hatred he and his new team will receive, Kiffin and LSU find a way.

Nick Saban is long retired, and Alabama can no longer run the football. Seriously, the Crimson Tide finished No. 125 in rushing yards last season, a figure that's hard to assess many months later.

But that was, after all, last season. Somehow, Alabama enters 2026 remarkably underrated, which is a statement one never thought to be possible.

We saw these two teams play twice last year. Alabama clipped Georgia on the road in a thriller early in the season. In the SEC Championship Game, the Bulldogs smothered the Crimson Tide 28-3. The lack of running game really showcased itself here for Kalen DeBoer's group.

A lot can change in a year, and Keelon Russell gets that conversation started. Everything I have heard out of Alabama regarding Russell has been overwhelmingly positive. If you're going to pick the Crimson Tide in this game, you must have faith in his ability to perform at a reasonably high level.

We believe that will happen and then some.

As for Georgia, there is plenty to like. The presumed conference favorite returns QB Gunner Stockton, who is wildly underrated. The rest of the roster has plenty to offer as well, which has become the norm.

On paper, this group feels like a more complete version than Alabama at the moment. But a brutal road trip coupled with a young quarterback poised to come into his own makes this a favorable spot for the home underdog.

October 17: Ohio State (-1.5) at Indiana

For the past two years, Indiana has defied history.

The Hoosiers matched one historic season by delivering one of the greatest college football campaigns ever a year later. And they did it with two different quarterbacks along with an experienced roster that was pieced together.

Perhaps Curt Cignetti will do it again. Doubting him—or at least betting against him—seems almost foolish at this point. But to simply assume Indiana will operate at the level it did last year despite losing so many key pieces feels unlikely.

It's not just losing a Heisman winner in Fernando Mendoza. It's losing key wide receivers, a shutdown cornerback and important contributors on both sides of the ball.

Oh, Indiana will still be good. This is not meant to mark the end. It's merely meant to acknowledge just how many good players are no longer there.

Ohio State knows this yearly ritual well. In fact, the Buckeyes lost plenty of talent off a team that had championship-level talent. The fact that quarterback Julian Sayin and wideout Jeremiah Smith remained, however, is a key difference-maker. And the emergence of running back Bo Jackson, a sophomore poised for an enormous season, is another theme to watch as well.

This doesn't have to be overly complicated. Ohio State and Indiana have coaches and players capable of winning a title, and that will be fully on display this season. But the Buckeyes feel more properly positioned a year later to win a challenging road game we can't wait to watch.

If the game we see this year is anything like the one we witnessed last season, we're in for a treat.

Miami won that game 27-24, although this was CJ Carr's first real taste of action. Also, this was played in Miami Gardens, which means we're heading to South Bend this time around.

Each side is talented at quarterback, but both must replace important NFL departures. Regardless of this matchup's result, Miami and Notre Dame have national-title aspirations.

For all the moving parts, and this game features plenty of them, the true X-factor is Darian Mensah. Miami's new quarterback will bring a dynamic that Carson Beck simply couldn't provide, and it will allow the Hurricanes' incredible array of weapons to reach new heights.

On the other side, Carr should be better. And even without Jeremiyah Love, the Notre Dame offense should still move the ball.

Defensively, both teams have a ton to offer. Both were top-10 in scoring defenses last season, and both should finish in a similar situation this fall.

Again, very similar. Tons to like. The difference is that this game will be played at Notre Dame, which is a meaningful edge for the Irish. But this current spread feels a tad too high, and a repeat of last season's nail-biter feels inevitable.

That's good news for college football and all of us.

articles.title: El Liverpool explica por qué no se van a poder enfrentar al Real Madrid en Anfield esta Champions
articles.standfirst: Las normas impiden que se puedan jugar tres veces seguidas el mismo partido en la fase liga
articles.summary: Las normas impiden que se puedan jugar tres veces seguidas el mismo partido en la fase liga
articles.body: El Liverpool ha anunciado hoy que de cara al sorteo de mañana jueves de la Liga de Campeones no podrá haber un Liverpool-Real Madrid en Anfield. La UEFA introdujo una normativa que pretende evitar que se repita el mismo partido en la fase de liga durante tres años consecutivos, por lo que al haberse jugado dos partidos en las dos últimas ediciones no podrá celebrarse en esta temporada. Sin embargo, el equipo de Andoni Iraola sí podrá jugar en el Bernabéu, ya los dos duelos anteriores fueron en el campo del Liverpool. Es decir, podrá haber un Real Madrid-Liverpool pero nunca un Liverpool-Real Madrid. El apartado 16.03 del reglamento de la Liga de Campeones de la temporada pasada decía: "La administración de la UEFA podrá determinar condiciones alternativas para el sorteo de acuerdo con los principios establecidos por el Comité de Competiciones de Clubes y podrá adaptar cualquiera de las condiciones del sorteo para evitar situaciones de empate y/o tener en cuenta cualquier limitación pertinente a la luz de las decisiones adoptadas por el Comité Ejecutivo de la UEFA". "El Comité de Competiciones de Clubes de la UEFA ha determinado una condición adicional que podría aplicarse al sorteo de la Liga de Campeones de la UEFA para la temporada 2026/27, decidiendo que ningún partido individual entre los mismos dos equipos podrá repetirse en la misma competición con el mismo equipo local durante tres temporadas consecutivas", añade. "Esto significa que si dos equipos que ya se enfrentaron en la fase de liga de la UEFA Champions League en la temporada 2024/25 vuelven a enfrentarse, jugando como locales, en la fase de liga de la UEFA Champions League en la temporada 2025/26, esos equipos no podrán volver a enfrentarse con el mismo equipo local en la temporada 2026/27", concluye. Hay otros dos partidos que no se podrán jugar en esta fase liga de la Champions: el Benfica-Juventus y el Inter-Arsenal, ya que ambos ya se han jugado dos veces seguidas en la fase liga de Champions.

articles.title: Cincuenta veces Pacheta
articles.standfirst: El técnico ha alcanzado el medio centenar de encuentros al frente del Granada con un equipo revitalizado; Bourama Dembele, renovado
articles.summary: El técnico ha alcanzado el medio centenar de encuentros al frente del Granada con un equipo revitalizado
articles.body: No podía imaginar José Rojo Martín 'Pacheta' lo que le deparaba el destino cuando estampó su firma en el contrato que le convertía en nuevo entrenador del Granada, una montaña rusa plagada de obstáculos e imprevistos que ha ido sorteando con pericia, manteniendo a flote un barco que, por momentos, parecía abocado al naufragio. El técnico burgalés llegó a Los Cármenes en una situación límite, con la misión de reengancharse a la lucha por el ascenso, una meta que se le escapó entre los dedos con la derrota ante el Racing, una 'cornada', como le gusta llamarlo a Pacheta, que aún escuece y que llevó al club andaluz a una situación límite, tanto en lo económico como en lo deportivo. Con numerosos impedimentos y una plantilla limitada, Pacheta afrontaba un nuevo curso al frente del Granada, sin torcer el gesto, manteniendo un optimismo contagioso, convirtiéndose en el faro del granadinismo en los pasajes más oscuros de la temporada, cuando el abismo se asomaba con una realidad. Tras construir un equipo competitivo, Pacheta logró esquivar la 'quema' con cierta tranquilidad. El verano tampoco iba a ser tranquilo, con un proceso de venta que casi se lleva por delante la planificación, pero parece que finalmente los engranajes han encajado y se ha podido formar un plantel competitivo, vitaminado con una hornada de canteranos que vienen pisando fuerte, una mezcla con la que el de Salas de los Infantes parece haber moldeado un equipo con carácter, listo para pelear por cotas más altas que la simple permanencia, como ha demostrado ante Oviedo y Mallorca, dos recién descendidos a los que se enfrentó sin complejos. En total, 50 encuentros, 47 de liga y 3 de Copa del Rey, al frente del Granada, con 17 victorias, 13 empates y una veintena de derrotas. Unas bodas de oro que llegan tras un periplo tumultuoso, en el que Pacheta ha sabido ser el guía del equipo, portavoz del club, el tutor de los jugadores y el terapeuta del granadinismo y todo respaldado con un trabajo incansable que ahora comienza a aflorar.

articles.title: Manchester City sign teenage Moroccan midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille
articles.summary: Sought-after Bouaddi joins the Premier League club on a five-year deal worth $117m.
articles.body:
Manchester City have signed teenage Moroccan midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille in a deal worth 100 million euros ($117m), the French club has confirmed.

Lille announced Bouaddi’s departure on a five-year deal on Wednesday, putting an end to ongoing speculation about the emerging talent’s future.

Ten-time Premier League champions Manchester City were in talks to sign Bouaddi after selling Rodri to Barcelona and Tijjani Reijnders to Al-Qadsiah, with Nico Gonzalez also poised to leave the Etihad.

Bouaddi was a crucial part of Morocco’s FIFA World Cup 2026 squad, showing a calm presence in the midfield as the Atlas Lions reached the quarterfinals of the tournament before falling to France.

Lille extended Bouaddi’s contract last year and, with three years remaining on the deal, they were expecting suitors to meet the 100 million euros (€117m) asking price.

“This is a very special day for me and my family,” Bouaddi said in a statement shared by City.

“Manchester City are, for me, the best club in the world.

“It’s a dream to be here and be able to call myself a City player. I have spent most of my life working hard to become the best player I can be and reach the top of the game.

“I’ve watched City for many years, and I love their style of play.

“City always try and play quality football. And they have shown they are winners – this Club feels like it’s built to win.”

Having risen through the French youth ranks, Bouaddi was tied to the French national team programme and marked as a future talent. Earlier this year, he became the youngest player to record 50 appearances in France’s top tier of club football – Ligue 1.

Being ahead of his time has been a theme throughout Bouaddi’s career. On the eve of his 17th birthday, in 2024, the rising star helped Lille secure a famous Champions League victory over Real Madrid.

On that special October night in northern France, Bouaddi faced a midfield comprising French internationals Eduardo Camavinga and Aurelien Tchouameni.

Football experts have repeatedly heaped praise on Bouaddi’s ability to soak up pressure and stand out as a midfield maestro for his club and country.

Bouaddi’s versatility can be seen on the pitch. Typically, holding midfielders are known for their defensive abilities – shielding the defence from the opposition’s attacks by cutting out passing lanes – but this young talent’s repertoire includes the ability to start an attack, too.

He is now the symbol of this new team and the rising star among Moroccan fans.

“He is amazing. What a talent, what a professional at 18 years of age,” Mohammed, a Morocco fan and the manager of Restaurante Jerusalem in Barcelona, Spain, told Al Jazeera in June.

“For those that slept instead of watching Brazil versus Morocco, they missed out on discovering the new [Sergio] Busquets,” Khalil Jadallah, a football commentator, said of Bouaddi’s talent.

“He can pass, he can defend, he can carry the ball, control the tempo … all this and he is only 18 years old.”

articles.title: Dani Sánchez y el Málaga separan sus caminos
articles.standfirst: Rescisión de contrato para el lateral malagueño
articles.summary: Rescisión de contrato para el lateral malagueño
articles.body: Dani Sánchez deja de ser jugador del Málaga CF después de que ambas partes hayan alcanzado un acuerdo para rescindir su contrato. La salida del lateral malagueño se ha hecho esperar algo más de lo previsto, pero el club de Martiricos ya ha hecho oficial el adiós a través de sus canales oficiales. La marcha del futbolista se produce después de varias semanas en las que su futuro estaba en el aire. Tal y como adelantó Radio MARCA Málaga, varios clubes de Segunda División como Córdoba, Cádiz, Sabadell y Eldense habían mostrado interés en su incorporación. A estas opciones se sumaban también propuestas procedentes del extranjero, concretamente de Portugal, Países Bajos y Alemania. Finalmente, ninguna de las alternativas ha terminado de cristalizar y Dani Sánchez abandona el Málaga para afrontar una nueva etapa lejos de La Rosaleda. El malaguismo ya tuvo la oportunidad de despedirse de él hace unos días. Tras el encuentro frente al Fulham, correspondiente al Trofeo Costa del Sol, La Rosaleda tributó una sonora ovación al lateral, que también fue manteado por sus compañeros sobre el césped. Dani Sánchez no pudo contener las lágrimas y dedicó unas palabras de agradecimiento a la afición y a todos los que le acompañaron durante su etapa como futbolista blanquiazul. El defensa malagueño se incorporó al primer equipo malaguista en la campaña 23/24, disputando un total de 29 partidos entre todas las competiciones y siendo parte del épico ascenso a Segunda en Tarragona. Las dos anteriores temporadas Dani Sánchez acumuló 41 encuentros oficiales más (39 de Liga y 2 de Copa) y, la pasada 25/26, logró un nuevo ascenso de categoría con el equipo, que regresaba a la élite del fútbol español ocho años después. Dani ha sido un pilar fundamental en el vestuario, aportando siempre tanto dentro como fuera del terreno de juego. Su personalidad, carisma y cercanía dejan una huella imborrable en la que siempre será su casa, La Rosaleda. Desde el Málaga CF queremos agradecer a Dani Sánchez por todo lo vivido y por formar parte de una etapa que ya es historia del Málaga CF con dos ascensos inolvidables.
